card.name: Word endings -ley and -ly in adverbs
card.fires_on: The ending piece "ley", "elsey" or "ly"/"edly"/"ely" when a word is split up, either in a surname (Kelsey, Besley, Brantley) or in an adverb before an adjective (dazzlingly complex, morbidly obese).

modes.label: Surname endings
modes.description: The last piece of a split surname ending in -ley or -elsey.
modes.example: Quin'yotae Brant<<ley>> smiles as she takes a bite out of

modes.label: Adverb endings
modes.description: The -ly, -edly or -ely ending of an adverb placed before an adjective.
modes.example: people with a missing copy of these genes are 43 times more likely to be morbid<<ly>> obese.

card.plain: It fires on the ending of a long name or a -ly adverb that has been broken into pieces.
